RECORDS.name: a sync export whose right-hand side merely began with `syncExport "NAME"` passed, so code sequenced after the application, outside syncExport's handler and scheduler run, went unreported
RECORDS.trigger: `lhSeq e = syncExport "lhSeq" (decide e) >>= dispatch` as a sync export's equation
RECORDS.ok: exit 1 with `FAIL lhSeq (A.hs:6): the equation of `lhSeq` at A.hs:4 is not `syncExport "lhSeq"` applied to its whole right-hand side`
RECORDS.bug: `ok   lhSeq (A.hs:6) is built on syncExport` and exit 0
RECORDS.notes: Found by the code review of 2026-10-23 over the year's diff. A prefix match stood in for reading where the application ends; the argument is now a `$` and what follows it, or one parenthesized expression or name with at most a `where` clause after it, the equation ending at the next line in column 0. The self-test's lhSeq and lhThen draw the finding and lhParen and lhNamed stay quiet; its mutant in tools/mutants.py restores the head-only match.
RECORDS.plant: a git repository whose one tracked file defines lhSeq as above and exports it sync
RECORDS.plant_cmd: git init -q . && printf '%s\n' 'module A where' '' 'lhSeq :: Int -> IO ()' 'lhSeq e = syncExport "lhSeq" (decide e) >>= dispatch' '' 'foreign export javascript "lhSeq sync" lhSeq :: Int -> IO ()' > A.hs && git add A.hs
RECORDS.expect_text: FAIL lhSeq (A.hs:6): the equation of `lhSeq` at A.hs:4 is not `syncExport "lhSeq"` applied to its whole right-hand side
RECORDS.bug_text: ok   lhSeq (A.hs:6) is built on syncExport

RECORDS.name: block comments did not nest: a `-}` closing an inner comment ended the outer one, so a commented-out sync export after it read as code
RECORDS.trigger: `{- outer {- inner -} still the outer comment` above a commented-out `foreign export javascript "lhNest sync"`
RECORDS.ok: the whole outer comment blanked: no sync export, exit 0
RECORDS.bug: `FAIL lhNest (A.hs:4): no equation of `lhNest`` and exit 1
RECORDS.notes: Found by the /simplify review of 2026-10-23, which compared this checker's comment blanker with ~/slop/tools/hssource.py's, which had fixed the same shape as hssource-03; the blanker now steps over pragmas and literals and nests block comments as that scanner does. Its mutant in tools/mutants.py restores the old behaviour.
